title: Chicken, broilers or fryers, drumstick, meat only, cooked, braised

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken drumsticks (broiler or fryer) without skin are the meat from the thigh portion of the bird, prepared by boiling and then braising. They have a tender flavor, soft texture, and high protein content, making them a popular ingredient in many dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Drumsticks are a staple in traditional cuisines worldwide, from Russian stews to Asian soups.
Braised drumsticks retain more B‑vitamins than fried ones, which are lost at high temperatures.
The thigh meat contains more iron than breast meat due to higher myoglobin levels.
When boiled, drumsticks release gelatin that enriches the broth’s body.
Chicken drumsticks are a good source of collagen, beneficial for skin and joint health.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports red blood cell formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: The iron in chicken meat is readily absorbed and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: Provides zinc
items.content: Zinc aids immune function and promotes wound healing.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Makes it suitable for low‑carb and keto diets.

items.title: Chicken meat allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If salt is added during cooking, the sodium level can become high, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked or improperly stored drumsticks may harbor Salmonella; proper temperature control is essential.

items.title: Higher cholesterol
items.content: Drumsticks contain more cholesterol than breast meat, so individuals with high cholesterol should monitor portions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drumsticks can be served as a main dish, added to salads, soups, stews, or used as a filling for pies. They are often split lengthwise along the bone to make eating easier.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked drumsticks in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a sealed bag for 2–3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before consumption.
